object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person seeking medical care at the clinic, identified by a unique patient ID that appears on their card.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments... Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical professional who sees patients in appointments and has a medical specialty, identified by a license number.

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled meeting between a patient and a doctor at a specific date and time slot, identified by an appointment number assigned when created.

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments... Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A physical room in the clinic where appointments take place, identified by a room number.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty

ambiguities.description: Optionality of VisitReason and FollowUpNote: The transcript states 'An appointment can have a visit reason' and 'the doctor can attach a follow-up note', using permissive language ('can'). However, it is unclear whether every appointment must have these or whether they are truly optional. For VisitReason: is it always provided by the patient, or only sometimes? For FollowUpNote: is it always required after a completed appointment, or only sometimes provided? The reverse direction is also unclear -- must every visit reason recorded be attached to exactly one appointment, or could a reason be recorded without being used?

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking, and after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note.

ambiguities.description: Scheduling constraints: The transcript specifies that each appointment is on one date and at one time slot, but does not explicitly state whether the same doctor can be double-booked in the same time slot or whether a room can host multiple appointments simultaneously. Are there uniqueness constraints on (Doctor, Date, TimeSlot) or (ExamRoom, Date, TimeSlot)? This could affect whether two patients can be seen by the same doctor at the same time.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

ambiguities.description: Relationship between AppointmentStatus values and temporal flow: The status values (scheduled, checked-in, completed, cancelled) suggest a workflow progression, but the transcript does not clarify the valid state transitions. For example, can a cancelled appointment be rescheduled, or must a new appointment be booked? Can an appointment transition from completed back to checked-in? This may not be a business rule needed for the conceptual model, but it affects how the status is interpreted.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.

ambiguities.description: ExamRoom participation: The transcript mentions that exam rooms have a room number, but does not explicitly state whether appointments are held in exam rooms, or whether the room assignment is required or optional. Is there a fact type connecting Appointment to ExamRoom? Should there be a constraint that each appointment occurs in exactly one room?

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

ambiguities.description: Primary doctor vs appointment doctor overlap: The transcript states that 'every patient has exactly one primary doctor' and 'That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.' This correctly identifies two distinct relationships, but does not clarify: (1) is the patient's primary doctor sometimes the doctor seen in an appointment, or are they always different? (2) can a patient see a non-primary doctor, or must they always see their primary doctor or only their primary doctor? The phrase 'separate' suggests they can differ, but the business rule governing when they differ is not explicit.

source_references.excerpt: Do patients have a regular doctor? Yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor. That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.
